reading.body:
Amazon Web Services recorded $717 billion in revenue in 2025 while operating two major AI product lines: SageMaker for full-stack ML lifecycle management and Bedrock for managed foundation model access.

AWS sits at the intersection of compute supply and AI demand. SageMaker's architecture—unified data lakes, model monitoring, bias detection, and governance tools—reflects the infrastructure required to run production AI at scale. Bedrock's API model with VPC support and IAM integration suggests AWS is positioning itself as the managed layer between foundation models and enterprise users who want isolation and control. Both products point to a company treating AI not as a feature but as a platform business spanning data, compute, and model serving.

The scale here matters for power and buildings. A $717 billion revenue company in cloud services operates data centers globally to deliver these products. The fact that SageMaker includes toxicity detection, guardrails, and data lineage tracking indicates AWS is building compliance and observability into the compute layer itself. This is not decorative. As regulatory exposure grows, the infrastructure provider that bakes governance into the platform gains advantage over those that bolt it on later.

The data does not specify AWS's capital spending, energy consumption, or data center locations. It does not break out AI revenue from total AWS revenue or show whether SageMaker and Bedrock are growing faster than legacy services. It does not name which foundation models Bedrock serves or how much compute AWS allocates to these two products versus others.

profile_text.body:
Amazon Web Services is a public company with ticker AMZN, founded in 1994, headquartered in Seattle, Washington, and reported revenue of $716,924,000,000 for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025. The company's website focuses on Amazon SageMaker, describing the next generation of SageMaker as "the center for all your data, analytics, and AI." It presents SageMaker Unified Studio as an integrated environment for analytics and AI, combining AWS machine learning and analytics tools, including SageMaker AI with HyperPod, JumpStart, and MLOps, and Amazon Q Developer, which the company calls "the most capable generative AI assistant for software development." The site also highlights a lakehouse architecture unifying Amazon S3 data lakes and Amazon Redshift data warehouses, with governance through Amazon SageMaker Catalog and support for open source frameworks on Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, and AWS Glue.

Amazon Web Services offers Amazon SageMaker, which provides full ML lifecycle management, model monitoring, bias detection, and explainability tools, and AWS Bedrock, a managed foundation model API service with IAM integration, VPC support, model evaluation tools, and AgentCore for agent orchestration. The company's site includes customer statements from an unnamed automotive operations unit and from Carrier about using SageMaker to unify data and accelerate analytics and AI development.

Amazon Web Services is a party in Haugland v. Anthropic PBC, a case in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. Washington state has 114 law exposure entries involving Amazon Web Services.
